note: These are optional reading sequences, not instructions for religious practice. Linked topic entries remain drafts until individually reviewed.

paths.title: Jainism: the basics
paths.description: Read about Jain beliefs, ahimsa, differences among Jain communities, and the path to liberation.
guiding_questions: Which ideas do Jain communities share, and where do their teachings differ?
How are knowledge, ethics, and spiritual practice related?

paths.title: Soul, karma, and liberation
paths.description: Read about the soul, karma, and Jain teachings on liberation from rebirth.
guiding_questions: What does Jain philosophy mean when it describes karma as subtle matter?
Why is a favorable rebirth different from liberation?

paths.title: Jain cosmology and cycles of time
paths.description: Read Jain accounts of loka, aloka, and the cycles of time.
guiding_questions: How do Jain texts describe loka and aloka?
What do the six eras describe in Jain cosmology?

paths.title: Ahimsa and Jain vows
paths.description: Read about ahimsa, Jain vows, and anekāntavāda, the idea that reality has many aspects.
guiding_questions: How do mendicant vows differ from lay vows?
How can different standpoints help explain why people disagree?

paths.title: Jain stories and history
paths.description: Read Jain stories about Rishabha, Bahubali, Mahavira, and Malli alongside historical accounts.
guiding_questions: What do Jain stories say about these figures, and what can historians establish?
Why do Jain accounts of Malli differ?

paths.title: Jain texts and communities
paths.description: Read about Jain scriptures, teachers, and community life.
guiding_questions: Why do Jain communities preserve different collections of scriptures?
How do monks, nuns, and lay Jains form the fourfold community?
